gaps.gap: Thin, low-authority content on the money page /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ — 335 impressions but position 33 and 0.3% CTR, while Tall.Life ranks with ~3,810 words and full Article/BreadcrumbList schema, and Wirecutter/BTOD dominate with 7,000–24,000+ words and structured data
gaps.recommendation: Expand /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ to 3,500–5,000 words targeting the tall-specific angle competitors miss (seat height ranges by height bracket, cylinder upgrades, seat depth requirements for 6'+ inseams). Add FAQ schema, Article schema, and a comparison table with chair dimensions. Target keywords: 'office chairs for tall people', 'best ergonomic chair for tall people', 'office chair for 6 foot person'. This is your highest-impression non-converting page and the fastest path to top-10.

gaps.gap: Missing structured schema on all review and comparison pages — /review/gesture/ has 649 impressions at position 10 with 0.15% CTR, but ChairsFX's Aeron review deploys Article, Person, ImageObject, BreadcrumbList, and WebPage schema, generating rich results that steal CTR even at lower positions
gaps.recommendation: Immediately implement Article, BreadcrumbList, Product, and Review/AggregateRating schema on /review/gesture/, /aeron-vs-gesture/, and /aeron-vs-leap-plus/. 649 impressions at position 10 with only 1 click is a schema/CTR problem, not a ranking problem. Also audit title tags on these pages — add tall-specific hooks like 'for Tall People (6'+)' or 'Tall Person Review' to differentiate from generic reviews and lift CTR organically.

gaps.gap: No tall-specific seat dimension content for the Herman Miller Aeron — /correct-chair-dimensions/ gets 532 impressions at position 23 with near-zero clicks, and /aeron-vs-gesture/ has strong impression volume (190–114), but there is no dedicated page covering Aeron sizing, size C vs B for tall people, or seat height/depth specs the way /chairs/steelcase-gesture/seat-depth/ and /chairs/steelcase-leap-plus/seat-height/ already attempt for Steelcase
gaps.recommendation: Build /chairs/herman-miller-aeron/tall-people/ and /chairs/herman-miller-aeron/seat-height/ to mirror the Steelcase sub-page pattern that is already generating impressions. Also overhaul /correct-chair-dimensions/ — at position 23 with 532 impressions it has ranking potential but needs a taller-person-specific angle, a measurement guide (seat height/depth/back height by user height), and internal links from the Aeron and Gesture review pages to consolidate topical authority around dimensions.

analysis.summary: Your site is generating meaningful impression volume across several high-intent pages but converting almost none of it into clicks, pointing to three compounding problems: under-built content on your most-searched money page, absent structured data that suppresses CTR even at solid positions, and an incomplete chair-specific sub-page architecture for the Aeron that leaves affiliate traffic on the table. The highest-ROI move this week is a combined content expansion and schema implementation sprint on /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ and /review/gesture/, as these two pages alone account for nearly 1,000 impressions with a combined 2 clicks. Closing the Aeron dimension content gap is the medium-term structural fix that will compound your topical authority and support the comparison pages already showing early ranking signals.
